newsitem.title: USA: US natgas producers used 93.3 pct capacity in 1995.
newsitem.headline: US natgas producers used 93.3 pct capacity in 1995.

text.p: U.S. natural gas producers used 93.3 percent of their fields' capacity in 1995, up from 91.1 percent in 1994, according to the Natural Gas Supply Association's final tally for last year.

NGSA's final deliverability study for 1995 showed even less surplus capacity than in preliminary results for 1995 released in July, which estimated that producers had used 92.4 percent of capacity in 1995.
The preliminary result covered 53 percent of lower-48 natural gas production compared with 59 percent covered by the final survey, including 82 percent off offshore production.
Maximum feasible capacity held steady at 94.6 percent, based on natural gas field capacity connected to pipelines.
Connected field capacity totalled 31 billion cubic feet a day at the end of 1995, off slightly from the previous year.

Spare capacity in offshore Gulf of Mexico fields shrank to 1.0 percent from 4.2 percent the previous year, while spare capacity in onshore Gulf fields, the Anadarko Basin, and East/North Central fields shrank to less than 1.0 percent.
In the Permian/San Juan Basin there was virtually no surplus capacity in 1995, compared with 2.2 percent in 1994, the NGSA survey said.
Out of seven main natural gas producing regions in the lower-48 states, Gulf of Mexico offshore fields delivered the most gas at 11.5 billion cubic feet a day, up 3.3 percent from 1994.
